name: Interpolation Methods
text:
# Interpolation Methods

Also called: Interpolation Schemes

## Overview
Interpolation Methods reconstruct continuous scalar fields from discrete voxel grids to determine values at arbitrary query positions during [ray casting](#6080-ray-casting.md) [S1, S2, unofficial]. They solve the problem of aliasing artifacts (staircase effects) inherent in nearest-neighbor sampling while avoiding the excessive blurring associated with low-pass filters [S1, S3, unofficial]. This family sets itself apart from sibling techniques like [Depth to Distance Conversion](2428-depth-to-distance-conversion.md) or [Alpha Grid Mask](2430-alpha-grid-mask.md) by focusing specifically on the spatial reconstruction kernel and weight calculation rather than sampling density or masking strategies.

## Shared principles
All methods in this family map a query position $\mathbf{p}$ in [voxel space](#3074-voxel-space.md) to a scalar value $V(\mathbf{p})$ by combining a finite set of neighboring voxel values $V_i$ using a set of weights $w_i(\mathbf{p})$:
$$
V(\mathbf{p}) = \sum_{i} w_i(\mathbf{p}) V_i
$$
The weights are derived from a reconstruction kernel $h(\mathbf{z})$, where $\mathbf{z}$ is the distance from the query point to the sample center [G]. The choice of kernel defines the trade-off between computational complexity, spatial extent (number of neighbors), and frequency response (aliasing vs. blurring) [S1, unofficial][S2, unofficial].

## Subtopics

### [Interpolation Schemes for Volume Rendering](817-interpolation-schemes-for-volume-rendering.md)
[Interpolation schemes for volume rendering](#817-interpolation-schemes-for-volume-rendering.md) define how scalar values are reconstructed at arbitrary query positions within a voxel grid to produce continuous images from discrete data. The core problem is balancing computational cost against visual fidelity, specifically mitigating aliasing artifacts (staircase effects) inherent in nearest-neighbor sampling while avoiding excessive blurring from low-pass filters. This family encompasses methods ranging from zeroth-order sample-and-hold to high-order frequency-domain sinc resampling, with specific implementations optimized for GPU hardware [acceleration](#18-acceleration.md) or spatial separability.

### [Gradient-Based Interpolation by Sample Splatting](9072-gradient-based-interpolation-by-sample-splatting.md)
[Gradient-Based Interpolation by Sample Splatting](#9072-gradient-based-interpolation-by-sample-splatting.md) is a real-time technique for reconstructing source radiance $L_x$ in inhomogeneous, single-scattering media by interpolating values and gradients from a sparse set of sample points. It solves the problem of severe rendering artifacts (e.g., in light shafts and volumetric shadows) that occur when standard interpolation methods, such as Radial Basis Functions (RBF), fail to capture sharp, high-frequency shading variations. Unlike RBF methods which assume [smooth shading](#4645-gouraud-shading.md), this method uses first-order Taylor approximations weighted by distance, enabling accurate reconstruction of local and directional illumination effects with significantly lower relative error (4.3% vs 14.7% for RBF) at comparable performance levels.

### [Shape-Based Interpolation](10499-shape-based-interpolation.md)
[Shape-Based Interpolation](#10499-shape-based-interpolation.md) (SBI) is a technique primarily used for surface rendering that preserves the geometric integrity of objects during the resampling process. Unlike standard scalar interpolation which blends voxel values and can distort boundaries, SBI operates by converting the object or surface into a continuous scene representation, interpolating that scene, and then extracting the resulting surface. This approach solves the problem of shape degradation (aliasing and blurring of edges) inherent in traditional volume rendering methods.

### [Lanczos Resampling](11246-lanczos-resampling.md)
[Lanczos resampling](#11246-lanczos-resampling.md) is an interpolation technique used to resample (downsample or upsample) volumetric data by replacing each selected sample with a translated copy of the Lanczos kernel, which is a limited Sinc function. It sets itself apart from linear or cubic interpolation by offering a sharper frequency response with reduced aliasing, at the cost of a wider support radius and higher computational complexity. It builds on [Interpolation Methods](10526-interpolation-methods.md).

### [Nearest Neighbor Sampling](11694-nearest-neighbor-sampling.md)
[Nearest Neighbor Sampling](#11694-nearest-neighbor-sampling.md) is a [voxel interpolation](#6486-voxel-interpolation-nearest-trilinear-triquadratic-tricubic.md) technique that retrieves the value of the single voxel whose integer coordinates are closest to the ray's current position. It serves as a fallback or low-cost alternative when higher-order interpolation is not required or when computational resources are constrained. Unlike trilinear interpolation, which combines neighboring samples to produce smoother results, Nearest Neighbor Sampling selects only the closest sample, resulting in lower image quality but significantly reduced execution time.

### Joseph's Method
Joseph's Method is a forward [projection method](#8336-projection-method.md) for 2D easily extended to 3D, using bi-linear interpolation on intersection points and a compensation factor for rays deviating from the principal direction [S2, unofficial]. To implement it, determine the principal direction of the ray by comparing the absolute differences $|x_1-x_2|$, $|y_1-y_2|$, and $|z_1-z_2|$. For the case where the principal direction is the x-axis ($|x_1-x_2|$ is largest), perform bi-linear interpolation on the intersection points of each $(y, z)$-plane of the sampling grid. Weight the sum of these interpolations with the factor $\frac{\sqrt{(x_1 - x_2)^2 + (y_1 - y_2)^2 + (z_1 - z_2)^2}}{|x_1 - x_2|}$ to compensate for the longer traversal of rays deviating from the principal direction [S2, unofficial]. Joseph's method performs similarly to Köhler's method in accuracy, despite using a skewed interpolation kernel compared to Köhler's tri-linear kernel [S2, unofficial].

### Interblock Interpolation
Interblock Interpolation is a technique to handle missing samples between blocks by interpolating from neighbors, allowing for higher data reduction [S3, unofficial]. The interpolated value is a normalized sum, $\phi$, of bounded block samples, $\phi_b$ [S3, unofficial]. With Interblock Interpolation, data reduction reaches 80:1 (1.25% of original data size) [S3, unofficial]. It also achieves data reduction of 40:1 to 50:1 (2% of original data size) [S3, unofficial].

### Higher-Order Interpolation via Template
Higher-Order Interpolation via Template is an extension of [template-based ray casting](#7802-ray-template-traversal.md) that uses connected cells instead of connected voxels to support higher-order interpolation by taking multiple samples along continuous rays within each cell [S4, unofficial]. To implement this, take multiple samples at regular intervals along the continuous ray inside each cell. Precompute part of the interpolation function and store it in a table to allow for faster rendering times [S4, unofficial].

## Background
Interpolation is a fundamental component of [direct volume ray casting](#19-direct-volume-ray-casting.md), introduced alongside early ray casting implementations to handle the mismatch between discrete voxel grids and continuous ray positions [S1, unofficial]. Nearest neighbor and trilinear interpolation were early standard methods, with trilinear offering improved image quality at the cost of substantial computational effort [S1, unofficial]. Forward projection methods like Joseph's method (1982) and Köhler's method (2000) were developed to improve accuracy in projection-based rendering, with Köhler separating volume construction from line-integration [S2, unofficial]. Shape-Based Interpolation emerged to address geometric fidelity issues in surface rendering [S1, unofficial]. Lanczos resampling was adopted for its superior frequency response compared to cubic interpolation [S1, unofficial]. Gradient-based [splatting](#23-splatting.md) was developed to handle complex lighting in inhomogeneous media where standard interpolation fails [S1, unofficial]. Interblock interpolation was introduced in the context of [GPU-based volume ray-casting](#7009-multi-pass-gpu-ray-casting-with-early-ray-termination.md) with advanced illumination to manage sparse data [S3, unofficial]. Higher-order template interpolation extended template-based rendering to support continuous value variation within cells [S4, unofficial].
